title: Integrable envelope for the first mean derivative
statement: Let $v>0$ and $M\ge 0$, and write $p_v(m,z)=(2\pi v)^{-1/2}\exp(-(z-m)^2/(2v))$ for the Gaussian density with mean $m$ and variance $v$. There is a Lebesgue-integrable function $b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that, for every $m,z\in\mathbb R$ with $|m|\le M$, $\left|\frac{z-m}{v}p_v(m,z)\right|\le b(z)$.
hypotheses_covered: $v$ is a nonzero nonnegative real, hence $v>0$
replaced: Let $v>0$ and $p_v(c,z)=(2\pi v)^{-1/2}\exp(-(z-c)^2/(2v))$. For every $M\ge0$, there exists a Lebesgue-integrable $b:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that $|((z-m)/v)p_v(m,z)|\le b(z)$ for all $z\in\mathbb R$ and all $m$ with $|m|\le M$.
